text:
Glioblastoma cells exploit glutamate via Ca2+-permeable AMPA receptors; Ca2+ influx phosphorylates Akt at Ser-473, driving proliferation and motility. Dominant-negative Akt blocked AMPA-receptor-accelerated proliferation/migration, while constitutively active Akt rescued apoptosis caused by converting receptors to Ca2+-impermeable via GluR2 cDNA. This glutamate-AMPA-Akt pathway may underlie anaplasia and invasive growth, offering a therapeutic target.

In mast cells, Ca2+ oscillations with accompanying Ca2+ entry through store-operated CRAC channels triggered gene expression, whereas oscillations without entry did not; increased buffering prevented oscillations but not gene activation. Local Ca2+ influx, not global oscillations, drives gene expression at physiological stimulation.

During LTP, synaptic incorporation of GluR1-containing AMPA receptors is controlled by a PKC phosphorylation site on GluR1.
